title: Community Garden Operations Worksheets
subtitle: Print these pages for your next planning session

pages.title: 1. Site walk-through
pages.intro: Use this before committing to beds, deliveries or a budget. Walk the site at more than one time of day and after rain if you can.
checks: Sun and shade are noted across the growing area.
Water source, hose reach and any usage limits are confirmed.
Access, slopes, muddy areas and turning space have been walked with intended users.
Land permission, site history and any recommended soil tests are understood.
Tool storage, delivery access and a safe gathering spot are identified.

pages.title: 2. Kick-off meeting and shared decisions
pages.intro: A one-page record helps new volunteers understand why the garden is being built and how decisions were made.
checks: Our two most important outcomes this season are written down.
We have named what is outside this season's scope.
We agreed how beds and harvests will be shared.
We know who can approve purchases and where receipts go.
We scheduled a review date rather than treating the first plan as permanent.

pages.title: 3. Volunteer rota and handover
pages.intro: Give each recurring task a named primary person, a backup and a simple handover. Avoid relying on one volunteer's memory.
checks: Watering instructions and water restrictions are visible near the equipment.
A backup contact is listed for each week.
Shared tools have a clear storage and return place.
Missed tasks can be reported without blame so the plan can be adjusted.

pages.title: 4. Harvest and surplus agreement
pages.intro: Decide the harvest rule before the first busy week. Check recipient requirements before promising a delivery.
checks: It is clear who may harvest and which crops are not ready yet.
The group has agreed how volunteer shares and community shares work.
A recipient has confirmed what produce, timing and handling they can accept.
Surplus and crop losses will be noted to improve next season's plan.
